With reference to above statements, which of the following applies ?
options: Statement I is true but II is false
Statement I is false but II is true

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
Statement 1 is true.

Consider statement 2

$\left [ D \right ]^{T}\left [ F \right ]\left [ D \right ]$ is always symmetric.

Now since

$$\begin{aligned} \left [ {D}'FD \right ]{}'&= {\left [ FD \right ]}'{\left ( {D}' \right )}' \\     &={\left ( FD \right )}'D \\     &={D}'{F}'D \\     &={D}'FD \end{aligned}$$

(Since F may or may not be symmetric)

$\therefore \;\; {D}'FD$ is not always symmetric is true.

$\therefore$ 1 is true and 2 is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2004:q13.title: GATE CE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 13
pp:ce:2004:q13.question: A 10 m thick clay layer is underlain by a sand layer of 20 m depth (see figure below). The water table is 5 m below the surface of clay layer. The soil above the water table is capillary saturated. The value of $\gamma _{sat}$ is 19 kN/$m^{3}$. The unit weight of water is $\gamma _{w}$. If now the water table rises to the surface, the effective stress at point P on the interface will

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown:
In first case, when the water table is 5m below the surface and the clay over water table is capillary saturated, the effective stress is given by

$$\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\gamma \times 5 \\ &=\gamma_{\text {sat }} \times 5+\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \; \; \; \ldots(i) \end{aligned}$$

In the second case, when water table rises to the surface, the effective stress is given by

$$\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\gamma \times 10=\left(\gamma_{\text {sat }}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \times 10 \\ &=10 \gamma_{\text {sat }}-10 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \\ &=\left(10 \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}\right)-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \quad[\because \text { from (i) }) \\ \Rightarrow \bar{\sigma}_{2} &=\bar{\sigma}_{1}-5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}$$

Thus in second case, the effective stress at the interface will decrease by $5 \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2004:q23.title: GATE CE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 23
pp:ce:2004:q23.question:
A wide channel is 1 m deep and has a velocity of flow, V, as 2.13 m/s. If a
disturbance is caused, an elementary wave can travel upstream with a velocity of

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
$F_{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{V}{C_{0}}=\frac{\text { Flow speed }}{\text { Wave speed }}$

At low speed, $F_{t} \lt 1;$ a small disturbance travels

u/s (with a velocity $C_{0}-V$ relative to a stationary

observer) and affects the u/s conditions.

At high flow velocities, $F_{r} \gt 1$, a small disturbance

travels d/s at a velocity of $\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{C}_{0}$ relative to a

stationary observer. (As $\mathrm{V} \gt \mathrm{C}_{0}$ small disturbance

can not travel u/s) and thus the u/s conditions

can not be influenced by the d/s conditions and

the flow is controlled by the u/s conditions.

Therefore, we can say that the region which

remains unaffected controls the flow.

$F_{r}=\frac{2.13}{\sqrt{9.81 \times 1}}=0.68 \lt 1$

(Subcritical flow)

$C_{0}=\sqrt{9.81 \times 1}=3.13 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$

An elementary wave travels u/s with a velocity $C_{0}-V$ relative to a stationary observer

$=3.13-2.13=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2004:q56.title: GATE CE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 56
pp:ce:2004:q56.question:
An unsupported excavation is made to the maximum possible depth in a clay

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Retaining Wall-Earth Pressure Theories
detailed_solution.markdown: The excavation is unsupported which means the maximum possible depth upto which the clay soil can be excavated is $2Z_{\mathrm{c}}$. The active earth pressure at this depth is $$\begin{aligned} P_{A} &=2 c \sqrt{K_{A}} \quad\left[\because K_{A}=\frac{1-\sin \phi}{1+\sin \phi}\right] \\ &=2 \times 100 \times \sqrt{\frac{1-\sin 30^{\circ}}{1+\sin 30^{\circ}}} \\ &=115.47 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively: $Z_{c}=\frac{2 c}{\gamma \sqrt{K_{A}}} \Rightarrow 2 Z_{c}=\frac{4 c}{\gamma \sqrt{K_{A}}}$ $\therefore$Active pressure at a depth, $2Z_{c}$ $$\begin{array}{l} =\gamma_{1} \times 2 Z_{c} \times K_{A}-2 c \sqrt{K_{A}} \\ =18 \times \frac{4 \times 100 \times \sqrt{3}}{18} \times \frac{1}{3} \\ \quad-2 \times 100 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ =230.94-115.47=115.47 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{array}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Retaining Wall-Earth Pressure Theories
detailed_solution.markdown:
Passive earth pressure for loose sand is

$$\begin{aligned} K_{p} &=\frac{1+\sin \phi}{1-\sin \phi}=\frac{1+\sin 30^{\circ}}{1-\sin 30^{\circ}}=3 \\ \text { Now } P_{P_{1}} &=\frac{1}{2} K_{P} \gamma H^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 17.8 \times 8^{2} \\ &=1708.8 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Passive earth pressure for compacted sand is

$$\begin{aligned} K_{P}&=\frac{1+\sin \phi}{1-\sin \phi}=\frac{1+\sin 35^{\circ}}{1-\sin 35^{\circ}}=3.69\\ \text { Now } P_{B} &=\frac{1}{2} K_{p} \gamma H^{2} \\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times 3.69 \times 18.8 \times 8^{2} \\ &=2219.90 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Ratio of $P_{P_{1}}$ and $P_{P_{2}}=\frac{1708.8}{2219.90}=0.77$

The bottom plate is stationery and the top plate moves with a steady velocity of V = 5 cm/s. The area of the plate is 0.25$m^2$.

The power required to keep the plate in steady motion is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Kinematics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Shear stress.

$\tau=\frac{\mu \partial U}{\partial y}=\frac{\mu V}{h}$

Shear force.

$F=\tau A$

Power required to keep the plate in steady motion

$$\begin{aligned} &=F \times\text{ Velocity}\\ &=\tau A \times V=\frac{\mu V}{h} \times A \times V \\ &=\frac{\mu V^{2} A}{h}=\frac{2 \times 10^{-4} \times\left(5 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{2} \times 0.25}{5 \times 10^{3}} \\ &=2.5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ Watts} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.
